title: Lesson 52 - Flow-Driven Data 360 Scenarios End to End: Read, Decide, Write Back
description: Use Data 360 in Salesforce flows, specifically an end-to-end, flow-driven scenario that reads unified data and writes a decision back, including testing, error handling, and governance.

questions.question: A Data Cloud-triggered flow fires on an engagement-score threshold but creates a Lead with blank fields. What should you check first?
options: Whether the running user has Modify All Data
Whether the Get Records element found the harmonized profile row (correct data space and conditions) and handled the no-records outcome
Whether the raw DLO is accelerated
Whether the data share is linked to its target
questions.explanation: Blank fields usually mean the Data 360 read returned no row or the no-records path was taken; the data space and conditions of Get Records are the first thing to verify.

questions.question: After you activate a new Data Cloud-triggered flow, nothing happens in the test, but the logic looks correct. What should you check first?
options: Rewrite the Start condition from scratch
The data stream refresh history, since flow output depends on refresh and on timing
Recreate the Data 360 connection and redeploy
Convert the flow to a screen flow
questions.explanation: Data Cloud-triggered flow timing depends on the data stream refresh schedule, so a delay is expected; confirm the refresh before changing logic that already looks right.

questions.question: Which split keeps a Data 360 plus flow design trustworthy?
options: Read unified data in the flow, decide, then write the decision to the CRM record
Write the decision back to Data 360 with an Update Records element
Read the data lake object and update the DMO from the flow
Do everything on the Run Immediately path for speed
questions.explanation: Flows read Data 360 and cannot write it, so the decision is written to the CRM record; reading a DLO and writing to the Run Immediately path both violate the element limits.
